successors.note: "Kano then became an emirate subject to Sokoto"; the dynasty was replaced by a Fulani one. The Kano Emirate Council survives as a non-sovereign monarchy in Nigeria.

capitals.note: Bagauda "took Sheme after defeating the rulers in 999 CE"; Sheme is not in the gazetteer and the coordinates are the Kano proxy.

capitals.name: Kano
capitals.note: Gijimasu (1095-1134) founded "a settlement at the foot of Dala Hill which would become Kano"; the infobox lists two capitals, 999 to 1095/1134 and 1095/1134 to 1805.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kano row). Bagauda took Sheme "after defeating the rulers in 999 CE"; the date "is arbitrary and approximate". No area on the page; a 40 km disc at Kano stands for the first core.

correction.text: the chiefdoms of the Kano plain, 'all of the chiefdoms in the area apart from Santolo' by 1200

keyframe_review.note: "By 1200, Kano had extended its rule over all of the chiefdoms in the area apart from Santolo"; drawn as the Kano State. Later reaches (Zazzau subdued under Kanajeji 1390-1410, tribute to Bornu from 1438-52 and to Kwararafa in slaves) are tributary or raiding relations the page does not outline and are not drawn.

ledger.note: c. 999: Bagauda takes Sheme and founds the Kano dynasty. "He took Sheme after defeating the rulers in 999 CE"; infobox "Established c. 999", the lead "around 1000 CE"; the date "is arbitrary and approximate".
1095: Gijimasu begins the city of Kano. "A settlement at the foot of Dala Hill which would become Kano" (reign 1095-1134); his son Tsaraki completed the walls.

ledger.note: 1807: the Sultanate of Kano ends. The infobox gives 1805 for the conquest in the jihad of Usman dan Fodio; the page has Alwali killed in 1807 (followed, as the Sokoto dossier dates the gain of Kano to 1807).

wars.name: Kano-Katsina wars
wars.outcome: Muhammad Rumfa's (1463-99) first war with Katsina "lasted 11 years and ended inconclusively"; under Abdullahi (1499-1509) and Muhammad Kisoki (1509-65) "despite the conquest of Zazzau it too ended inconclusively".
wars.note: No border change; years are the reigns the page gives.

wars.name: Kano and Zazzau
wars.outcome: Kanajeji (1390-1410) "subdued Zazzau, killing its king in battle"; the page does not make Zazzau a lasting part of Kano.

wars.name: Fulani jihad against Kano

wars.outcome: Muhammadu Bakatsine rebelled against Alwali; Alwali was deposed in 1805 and killed in 1807 and Kano became an emirate of Sokoto.

certainty.note: No frontier on the page; the Hausa state was a walled city with a plain around it, and its tributaries are not outlined.

sources.title: Kano Sultanate
sources.note: Identity, c. 999 founding, Gijimasu 1095, 1200 consolidation, Yaji, Kanajeji, Bornu tribute 1438-52, Rumfa, Katsina wars, 1805/1807; no area.

notes:
Sultanate of Kano (Kingdom of Kano), additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row. Page: Kano Sultanate; the Hausa Kingdoms page (opened) gave no founding dates for the Hausa states and is not cited.

End 1807 (Alwali killed) versus infobox 1805; the Sokoto dossier dates the gain of Kano to 1807. The page gives no area; Kano State stands for the plain, and neither the Zazzau conquest under Kanajeji nor the tribute to Bornu (from 1438-52), to Songhai/Kebbi (not on the page) and to Kwararafa (in slaves) is drawn. Kano's Bornu tribute is a vassal tie for the empire-of-kanem dossier (not drawn there either).
Counterparts: sultanate-of-katsina, zazzau (no dossiers yet), sokoto-caliphate (exists). Gazetteer: Sheme, Santolo, Kano admin1 exists.
